expect_nodes.name: mytool
expect_nodes.note: INTENDED: the BINARY name, declared in pyproject.toml `[project.scripts] mytool = ...`. EXPECTED to miss — cli.rs reads decorator/struct literals only, never the packaging manifest. This is the half that makes the pairing below impossible.

expect_edges.note: INTENDED: the invoker's `mytool` pairs with the declared binary. CliInvocationResolver joins `cli_invoke:<tool>` to `cli:<tool>` by EXACT tool name, so this needs both the binary declaration (absent: pyproject [project.scripts] is not read, LA.20) and a captured invocation (present since A13.4, see python/cli_inv). The invocation's subcommand pass pairs `cli_invoke:mytool -> cli:sync` (Weak), which this key does not assert.

forbid.name: cli

forbid.name: sync-records
forbid.note: precision: the docstring/help text is not a command name

note: A15.11 measured the thinly-covered cli_def column. Baseline 2026-09-16 on the installed 0.4.18 wheel: 6 nodes / 3 edges. The review's prediction — 'declarations are subcommands but invocations are binaries so they never pair' — holds for PYTHON, and the root cause is precise: click declares `sync`, the binary name lives only in pyproject.toml, and cli.rs never reads it. Contrast go/cli_def, where cobra's rootCmd DOES carry the binary name and the pairing fires.
